items.followUp: Explain how biology is related to chemistry and mathematics through two interdisciplinary sciences.

rubric.why: Award for correctly naming biophysics and relating it to physics and living organisms.
rubric.description: Biophysics applies principles of physics to biological processes.
rubric.how: Look for the term biophysics and its connection to physics or biological processes.

rubric.why: Award for correctly relating biochemistry to chemistry in organisms.
rubric.description: Biochemistry studies chemical substances and reactions in living organisms.
rubric.how: Look for biochemistry and a reference to chemical substances or reactions in organisms.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the use of mathematics or statistics in biology.
rubric.description: Biometry uses mathematics and statistics to analyse biological data.
rubric.how: Look for biometry connected to mathematics, statistics, or biological data.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the use of computers to handle biological information.
rubric.description: Bioinformatics uses computers to store and analyse biological data.
rubric.how: Look for bioinformatics connected to computers or biological information.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the practical use of organisms or biological processes.
rubric.description: Biotechnology uses organisms or biological processes to make useful products.
rubric.how: Look for biotechnology and its use of organisms or biological processes for a useful purpose.

modelAnswer: Biophysics applies the principles of physics to living organisms and their processes.
Biochemistry studies the chemical substances and reactions occurring in organisms.
Biometry uses mathematics and statistics to measure and analyse biological data.
Bioinformatics uses computers to store and analyse biological information.
Biotechnology uses organisms or biological processes to make useful products.

items.followUp: Define ATP and state how its three phosphate groups are attached to adenosine.

rubric.why: Award for expanding ATP and identifying its role in energy transfer.
rubric.description: ATP is adenosine triphosphate, the energy currency of the cell.
rubric.how: Look for the full name or the term energy currency.

rubric.why: Award for correctly identifying the components of adenosine.
rubric.description: Adenine combined with ribose forms adenosine.
rubric.how: Look for adenine, ribose, and their combination as adenosine.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the three phosphate groups in ATP.
rubric.description: Adenosine is joined to three phosphate groups.
rubric.how: Look for three phosphate groups or the term triphosphate.

rubric.why: Award for a correct labelled structural representation showing adenosine and three phosphates.
rubric.description: Structure: adenine—ribose—P—P—P (three phosphate groups attached to adenosine).
rubric.how: Check that the drawing or written structure shows adenine, ribose, and three linked phosphate groups.

modelAnswer: ATP (adenosine triphosphate) is the cell’s energy-carrying molecule, often called its energy currency.
Adenine joined to ribose forms adenosine.
Adenosine is joined to three phosphate groups to form ATP.
Structure:  Adenine — Ribose — P ~ P ~ P  (P = phosphate group; three phosphate groups)

items.followUp: Describe hypertension and atherosclerosis, and state one possible result of a blocked coronary artery.

rubric.why: Award for describing fatty plaque deposition in arteries.
rubric.description: Atherosclerosis is the build-up of fatty deposits or plaques in artery walls.
rubric.how: Look for the named disorder and fatty deposits or plaque in arteries.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the effect of arterial narrowing.
rubric.description: Plaques narrow arteries and reduce blood flow.
rubric.how: Look for narrowing of arteries or reduced blood flow.

rubric.why: Award for correctly defining hypertension.
rubric.description: Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure.
rubric.how: Look for hypertension linked to high blood pressure.

rubric.why: Award for linking blockage of a coronary artery to a heart attack.
rubric.description: A blocked coronary artery can cause a heart attack by cutting off blood supply to heart muscle.
rubric.how: Look for a heart attack or myocardial infarction linked to coronary blockage.

modelAnswer: Atherosclerosis is the build-up of fatty deposits (plaques) in the walls of arteries.
These deposits narrow the arteries and reduce blood flow.
Hypertension is persistently high blood pressure.
If a coronary artery is blocked, the heart muscle may lose its blood supply and a heart attack may occur.

items.followUp: State five ways fertilizers benefit crop plants or agricultural production.

rubric.why: Award for stating that fertilizers supply essential plant nutrients.
rubric.description: Fertilizers provide essential nutrients needed by plants.
rubric.how: Look for fertilizers supplying or providing nutrients.

rubric.why: Award for naming a major nutrient supplied by fertilizers.
rubric.description: Fertilizers supply important mineral nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, or potassium.
rubric.how: Look for at least one major plant nutrient.

rubric.why: Award for stating that fertilizers maintain or improve soil fertility.
rubric.description: Fertilizers replenish nutrients and improve soil fertility.
rubric.how: Look for improved or replenished soil fertility.

rubric.why: Award for connecting fertilizer use with improved plant growth.
rubric.description: Fertilizers promote healthy growth and development of plants.
rubric.how: Look for improved or healthy plant or crop growth.

rubric.why: Award for stating the benefit to agricultural production.
rubric.description: Fertilizers can increase crop yield and food production.
rubric.how: Look for increased crop yield or production.

modelAnswer: Fertilizers supply plants with essential mineral nutrients.
They provide important nutrients such as nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium.
They replenish nutrients in the soil and help maintain soil fertility.
They promote healthy growth and development of plants.
They can increase crop yield and food production.

items.followUp: Give two examples of how horticulture benefits people in their homes or communities.

rubric.why: Award for one application involving the cultivation of useful food plants.
rubric.description: Horticulture provides fruits and vegetables for food.
rubric.how: Look for growing or supplying fruits or vegetables.

rubric.why: Award for a second valid daily-life application of horticulture.
rubric.description: Horticulture is also used to grow flowers or ornamental plants, landscape places, or cultivate medicinal plants.
rubric.how: Look for a valid application other than food cultivation, such as flowers, landscaping, or medicinal plants.

modelAnswer: Horticulture is used to grow fruits and vegetables for food.
It is also used to grow flowers and ornamental plants for gardens and landscaping.

items.followUp: Name four organisms that belong to kingdom Monera.

rubric.why: Award for naming a valid unicellular organism.
rubric.description: Any two correct examples of unicellular organisms.
rubric.how: Award this mark for any two valid examples, including bacteria, Amoeba, Paramecium, Euglena, or yeast.

rubric.why: Award for the remaining two correct examples.
rubric.description: Any two further correct examples of unicellular organisms.
rubric.how: The response must name four examples in total; accept any four valid examples, including Amoeba, Paramecium, Euglena, yeast, or bacteria.

modelAnswer: Bacteria, Amoeba, Paramecium, and Euglena are four unicellular organisms.

items.followUp: Give one example each of a quantitative and a qualitative observation.

rubric.why: Award for defining a quantitative observation as one involving numbers or measurement.
rubric.description: A quantitative observation is expressed using numbers or measurements.
rubric.how: Look for a definition that explicitly mentions numerical data, counting, or measurement.

rubric.why: Award for defining a qualitative observation as a description of qualities without numerical measurement.
rubric.description: A qualitative observation describes qualities or characteristics and is not expressed numerically.
rubric.how: Look for a description of qualities or characteristics, with no reliance on numerical measurement.

modelAnswer: A quantitative observation is based on numbers or measurements, for example, a plant is 12 cm tall.
A qualitative observation describes qualities or characteristics, for example, a flower is red.

items.followUp: State two differences between organisms of kingdom Monera and kingdom Protista.

rubric.why: Award for identifying the prokaryotic cell organisation of Monera.
rubric.description: Monerans are prokaryotic and lack a true, membrane-bound nucleus.
rubric.how: Look for prokaryotic or the absence of a true nucleus.

rubric.why: Award for one further correct characteristic of Monera.
rubric.description: Monerans are unicellular; they may have a cell wall and commonly reproduce by binary fission.
rubric.how: Look for a correct additional characteristic such as unicellularity, a cell wall, binary fission, or absence of membrane-bound organelles.

modelAnswer: Organisms of kingdom Monera are unicellular and prokaryotic.
Their cells lack a true, membrane-bound nucleus; many have a cell wall and reproduce by binary fission.
